audit.why: Both layers already read Quinn, Rumble, Rumble, Skill, Skill, Rumble, Rumble — exactly the chart the audited mirror settled on. The packet's chart (Quinn six times, then Rumble) disagrees with the mirror AND with a 54.44% win rate that is earned early and lost late.
audit.corrected: NO chart edits proposed. The two layers already agree with each other and with the mirror; introducing the packet's version would break the mirror and contradict every why on the page.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page conflates Danger Zone with Overheat — wants.foe[1] literally reads 'Reach overheat (the Danger Zone)', and three other strings describe an 'overheated Flamespitter' melting you. It also calls Electro Harpoon 'short'-ranged, twice.
audit.why: Riot text for Junkyard Titan: Danger Zone is 50% Heat and empowers his basic abilities; at 100% Heat he Overheats, gains attack speed and on-hit damage but is UNABLE TO CAST SPELLS. So an overheated Rumble cannot use Flamespitter at all — the state the page warns you about is the one window you should be all-inning into. Electro Harpoon is 850 range on a 0.5s cooldown with two charges, longer than Quinn's basic attack range — describing it as short tells the player they are safe where they are not. It also reduces magic resist, which undercuts the page's own 'build MR' advice.
audit.corrected: Danger Zone and Overheat separated everywhere, with Overheat written in as Quinn's free all-in window. Electro Harpoon given its real 850 range, two charges and the MR shred. Flamespitter given its 600-range, 3-second cone and its 10/9/8/7/6s.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Build MR' is a do, and Mercury's Treads is the boot recommendation, with no mention that his harpoons strip magic resist.
audit.why: Electro Harpoon reduces MR per hit and he carries two charges — MR is still correct but it is not a solution on its own, and the page presented it as one.
audit.corrected: dosFull[1].d now states the shred alongside the buy.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 you convert poke into plates and a shove. Keep baiting him to step up for CS, then E-W-Q burst him — his only answer is heat-management, and a non-overheated Rumble loses the trade to your sustained Harrier autos. At 6 your R is for roam, not the duel: shove the wave and skystrike into a side lane to tax another matchup while he's stuck farming. Just remember his Flamespitter ignores your Q blind since it's ability damage, so don't try to facetank his flames — kite them.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 you convert poke into plates and a shove. Keep baiting him to step up for CS, then Vault-W-Q burst him — his only answer is heat management. Watch the bar: at 100% heat he Overheats and cannot cast a single spell until it drains, and that is your free all-in window. At 6 your R is for roam, not the duel: shove and skystrike into a side lane while he farms. And remember Flamespitter ignores your blind — it is ability damage, so kite the cone instead of facetanking it.

edits.before: This is where Rumble flips it. By two-plus items his Equalizer carpets any fight and his overheated Flamespitter plus Liandry's/Rylai's burn through your squishy frame, and you have no AoE or front-to-back threat to answer it. Your job was to win the game on the map before this point — split with R, pick off his isolated carries, and never walk into a teamfight through his ult zone. If it goes long, you're a flank-and-pick threat, not a frontline duelist.

notes: DATA CONFLICT, LEFT AS-IS DELIBERATELY: the packet's levelChart for this matchup reads Quinn x6 then Rumble, but the audited rumble side settled on Quinn / Rumble / Rumble / Skill / Skill / Rumble / Rumble, and BOTH layers of this page already hold that second version in agreement with each other. I proposed no chart edits — following the packet would have broken the mirror and contradicted the page's own whys, which describe Rumble owning levels 2-3 and the late game. Someone should decide which source wins before the next pass. THE BIG FIX: the page told the player to fear an 'overheated Flamespitter'. Overheat means he cannot cast spells at all — that is the window to kill him, not to run from. Also corrected Electro Harpoon from 'short range' to its real 850 with two charges and MR shred, which is what actually punishes a Quinn holding her ground. NOT FIXED (under the applier's 25-character skip): focus.text reads 'Rumble Scrap Shield' at 19 characters. The matchup-defining ability is Flamespitter, not a 6-second self-shield, so the loading screen and the focus card still point at the wrong ability. That needs a mechanical fix outside a length-banded edit. SUSPECTNAME: 'Drop Equalizer' was a genuine near-miss — the ability is 'The Equalizer', now corrected.
